data.title: Abbott in $385M settlement with DOJ over infant formula recall
data.description:
Abbott Laboratories (ABT) has agreed to pay the Department of Justice $385M to resolve claims related to its 2022 recall of baby formula manufactured at a Michigan plant in which deadly bacteria allegedly killed two infants.

The company has admitted no wrongdoing, and the settlement does not represent an admission of guilt.

Abbott was facing a criminal investigation from the DOJ as well, but that was dropped in June. 

The federal government's civil complaint alleged that it bought Abbott formula for government programs "despite the products' failure to meet statutory, regulatory, and contractual requirements," according to a news release. "The Complaint alleged that Abbott knowingly manufactured infant formula purchased with taxpayer dollars in an environment that put the products at unacceptable risk of microorganism contamination and significantly impacted the products' reliability, quality, and safety."

The complaint described conditions at the Sturgis, Mich., facility, including roof leaks. "Rather than permanently addressing the root causes, Abbott used temporary solutions, such as roof leak umbrellas, to try to divert leaks in product processing areas even though Abbott corporate leadership understood that the wet environment put the products at increased risk of microorganism contamination."

Of the $385M settlement, $348,700,868 will go to the feds to address False Claims Act allegations while $36,298,172 will go to some states for claims related to their Medicaid and WIC programs.

Abbott said that "no unopened, distributed Abbott infant formulas have ever tested positive for Cronobacter sakazakii."

"We make infant formula with the same care we would for our own families and are deeply committed to earning and maintaining caregivers' trust," the company stated.

data.title: Costco hikes motor oil prices and limits purchases
data.description:
Costco Wholesale (COST) has sharply raised the price of its Kirkland Signature full-synthetic motor oil and introduced purchase limits as lubricant supplies tighten. The 10-quart package from the retailer, which contains two 5-quart bottles, now sells for about $57.99, almost double the prior range of $30 to $35. 

Members are generally limited to two packages per week, with some local listings indicating a limit of one purchase transaction at a time. Costco (COST) has also reportedly imposed limits on Mobil 1 full-synthetic six-quart packs, which sell for around $44.

Other major sellers of motor oil such as Walmart (WMT), Amazon (AMZN), and AutoZone (AZO) do not appear to have followed Costco (COST) yet in significantly hiking motor oil prices or limiting purchases.

The move is unusual for the retailer since bulk availability is in its DNA. Repercussions from rising crude oil prices and broader lubricant shortages associated with disruptions in petroleum markets and shipping are believed to have factored into the price boost. The Costco (COST) chain was also ground zero for the great toilet paper scare of the early days of the pandemic in 2020.

Shares of Costco (COST) were up 1.4% in Monday afternoon trading.

data.title: AI infrastructure: Where cloud, power, and grid demand converge
data.description:
Investors Should Know: AI infrastructure is reshaping how investors think about a wide range of sectors, from cloud computing and data centers to power generation and internet services. The buildout required to train and deploy AI models is creating investment exposure across multiple business models, some directly tied to compute capacity and others connected through energy and grid infrastructure.

Key Takeaways

  • AI data-center expansion is creating demand that touches multiple sectors simultaneously, including cloud infrastructure, power generation, and internet services, each with different risk and return profiles.
  • Utilities are increasingly being viewed as potential beneficiaries of AI-driven power demand, shifting their traditional role from purely defensive income plays toward businesses with growth exposure.
  • Long-term power agreements and grid investment are among the mechanisms through which utilities could participate in AI infrastructure growth, though regulatory resistance and interest-rate sensitivity remain key risks.
  • The gap between announced AI infrastructure pipelines and what ultimately gets built is a central uncertainty for investors assessing this theme across sectors.
  • Analyst coverage skews cautiously bullish on AI infrastructure exposure, with bulls pointing to structural power demand as a durable tailwind and bears flagging governance uncertainty and buildout execution risk.

Background: How AI Infrastructure Demand Connects Cloud, Power, and Internet Services

Building and running AI models requires computing capacity and electricity. Data centers house the hardware needed for AI workloads, and that hardware draws substantial amounts of power. This creates a supply chain that spans cloud providers, data-center operators, and the utilities and grid infrastructure that keep those facilities running.

Utilities have historically been valued as stable, low-growth income investments. The growth in AI-related power demand is prompting a reassessment of that role. If data-center loads continue expanding, utilities with exposure to those loads through long-term power agreements or grid investment could see earnings growth that looks less like a traditional utility and more like a participant in the AI buildout.

Internet services and infrastructure companies occupy a related but distinct part of this ecosystem. These businesses provide the connectivity, content delivery, and cloud-adjacent services that sit between data centers and end users. Their exposure to AI infrastructure growth varies significantly by business model.

Stocks to Watch

CoreWeave, Inc. (CRWV) is a specialized GPU cloud provider focused on high-performance computing infrastructure used in AI model training and deployment. It represents one of the larger pure-play AI cloud names in the space by market capitalization.

Other companies in the AI Cloud and HPC category include TeraWulf Inc. (WULF), WhiteFiber, Inc. (WYFI), Cipher Digital Inc. (CIFR), HIVE Digital Technologies Ltd. (HIVE), IREN Limited (IREN), CleanSpark, Inc. (CLSK), Core Scientific, Inc. (CORZ), GDS Holdings Limited (GDS), and VNET Group, Inc. (VNET). These names span data-center operators, digital infrastructure providers, and compute-focused businesses across different geographies and market cap sizes.

Within internet services and infrastructure, Fastly, Inc. (FSLY), Backblaze, Inc. (BLZE), and VTEX represent companies in the broader connectivity and cloud-adjacent services segment carrying current Buy or Strong Buy Quant Ratings.

News Roundup

  • Cain Lee argues that AI data-center power demand could reshape utility earnings, with long-term power agreements and grid investment as the primary mechanisms through which utilities may benefit from expanding AI loads.
  • The same analysis distinguishes between the Defiance AI & Power Infrastructure ETF (AIPO), which targets AI hardware, data centers, and power infrastructure, and the Utilities Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLU), which provides exposure to established utilities serving data-center demand.
  • Preeti Singh reports that Bridgewater co-chief investment officer Greg Jensen warned that rapid AI development could outpace oversight and create significant societal risks, introducing uncertainty around the pace and form of future AI deployment.

data.title: SkyShowtime may be sold or shut down - reports
data.description:
Comcast (CMCSA) and Paramount Skydance (PSKY) are starting a review of strategic options for SkyShowtime, their European joint venture streaming service.

No decisions have been made, but shuttering the business is one of the options being considered, according to several media outlets, including Hollywood Reporter. The board of SkyShowtime informed its CEO, Monty Sarhan, of the review Monday in a letter that was viewed by the publication.

“SkyShowtime’s shareholders are commencing a review of strategic options for the business, which includes the possibility of a wind down," according to the letter. "No decisions have been made, and all options remain under consideration.”

SkyShowtime combines content from NBCUniversal and Sky Studios as well as Paramount.

data.title: Vista Equity looking at options for financial software provider Finastra - report
data.description:
Private equity ‌shop Vista Equity Partners is exploring strategic options for Finastra, which could include a possible sale of the financial sofware provider. 

The PE firm is working with bankers at Morgan Stanley on the review processs, which is in its early stages and could include a sale of compnay, or Vista selling a stake in Finastra or the company combining with another industry player, according to a  Reuters report on Monday, which cited people familiar with the matter.

London-based Finastra has attracted initial interest from parties including other financial sponsors, according to the report. Blackstone (BX) is among possible bidders looking at the firm.  

Vista, Finastra, Morgan Stanley and Blackstone all declined to comment to Reuters.

One person familiar told Reuters Finastra could be worth as much as $12 billlion in a sale. The companty is forecast to generate $650 million in EBITDA this year.

data.title: Google considers new data center in energy-rich Lea County, N.M.
data.description:
Google (GOOG)(GOOGL) is considering building a new data center project in Lea County, N.M., and is focused on community outreach as a key part of the development.

"Our goal in Lea County is simple: serve as long-term partners who can be counted on to do the right thing in support of the places we call home," Google said in a blog post about the proposed project. "That includes responsibly managing vital water resources, paying for 100% of the energy we use and infrastructure we need, and showing up as active members of the community."

Google indicated that it recognizes the pushback in many communities regarding data center development, so it intends to begin the conversation with locals.

The county is located in the western portion of the Permian Basin, which produces high volumes of oil, natural gas and natural gas liquids. The area has significant gas-fired power generation and infrastructure. For years, though, oil and gas operators in this region have flared, or burned off, natural gas as they target the higher-value oil. The region has seen gas spot prices hit negatives due to the glut of natural gas associated with shale oil production.

data.title: FX weekly: Greenback strengthens as markets brace for tighter Fed policy
data.description:
The dollar index (DXY), which measures the greenback against a basket of major currencies, was last up 0.29% at $99.41 and remains up about 1.34% for the year to date.

Dollar weekly moves and key drivers:

Over the past week, the index added 0.51%,as as the US dollar strengthened as Treasury yields surged following stronger-than-expected US producer inflation, boosting expectations of a Federal Reserve  rate hike next week.

The dollar was also supported by lower-than-expected Treasury purchases in its first expanded buyback operation.

Meanwhile, oil prices rose above $100 a barrel amid escalating Middle East tensions, fueling inflation concerns and expectations of prolonged tight monetary policy.

U.S. Treasury yields were mixed over the week, with the 10-year yield (US10Y) adding 20 basis points to 4.98%, while the 2-year yield (US2Y) advanced 26 basis points to 4.63%.

Currency Highlights:

Major currency movements (Sep. 7 to Sep. 13)

Euro (EUR:USD)

-0.46%

Pound Sterling (GBP:USD)

-0.24%

+0.04%

-1.06%

-0.93%

-0.47%
 

The Euro (EUR:USD) was last down 0.35%, as the dollar remained supported. The European Central Bank raised rates by 25 basis points last week, warning that inflation is likely to remain well above its 2% target for an extended period. 

The Swiss Franc (CHF:USD) was last down 0.21%. It weakened to a one-month low in the last week on a widening interest rate differential with the US, and new carry trades increased selling pressure. A hawkish Bank of Japan stance and yen-buying interventions by Washington and Tokyo reduced the yen’s appeal, prompting traders to shift toward other safe-haven currencies, such as the Swiss franc.

data.title: Chevron says exploring opportunities on four continents in LNG expansion drive
data.description:
Chevron (CVX) is looking to expand its natural gas portfolio in Argentina, the eastern Mediterranean, Africa, and Australia to meet growing demand from buyers concerned about energy security due to the crisis in the ‌Middle East, the company's President of Global Gas Freeman Shaheen said on Monday.

"What we're ​seeing from this crisis is that it just reinforces the need for diversity - diversity of supply and diversity of ​different contracting structures... and not leaving yourselves susceptible to a spot market that's not really ⁠as liquid as crude and products," Shaheen told Reuters on the sidelines of the Gastech conference in Bangkok.

Chevron (CVX) will have ~20M metric tons/year LNG supply capacity consisting of 16M tons of net gas production from its projects and 4M tons contracted from the U.S. Gulf Coast that began in February and ramp up over the next few years in line with agreements, and "we're looking to continue to expand that portfolio," Shaheen said.

There are "great prospects out of Argentina with the development of crude and gas ​in that marketplace," Shaheen said, referring to expansion in the Vaca Muerta shale play, while not elaborating on where in Africa, Australia, or the Mediterranean the company might expand.

Chevron (CVX) is considering investing in European LNG import capacity but needs greater clarity on the bloc's methane rules before making a long-term commitment, the executive said.

Europe's reliance on LNG imports from the U.S. and elsewhere has surged since Russian supply was lost following the invasion of Ukraine in 2022, but investing further in the infrastructure that supports such imports requires having greater clarity on the continent's methane rules, Shaheen said.

Under the European Union's latest proposal, fossil fuel imports will have to comply with monitoring, reporting, and verification requirements aimed at reducing methane emissions, and imports exceeding a certain methane-intensity threshold will face penalties starting in 2030.

data.title: Estée Lauder partners with Profound to expand AI-powered brand discovery
data.description:
• Estée Lauder (EL) is partnering with AI marketing platform Profound to help the company see how its brands appear across generative AI platforms and identify ways to improve visibility.
  • By using Profound’s findings, Estée Lauder (EL) can optimize content across social media and product description pages, ensuring product information, ingredients, claims, and benefits are optimized for consumer visibility and easier for large language models to understand and surface to consumers.
  • “The way people discover beauty is being rewritten in real time, and we intend to shape that shift rather than reacting to it,” said Aude Gandon, Estée Lauder’s global chief digital & marketing officer.   
  • Adds Profound’s CEO and co-founder James Cadwallader: “Enabling this strategy at scale across an entire prestige beauty portfolio sets a new bar for what enterprise AI visibility strategy looks like in this category.”

data.title: Frequency Electronics downgraded at Freedom Broker on valuation
data.description:
Frequency Electronics (FEIM) was downgraded to Hold from Buy at Freedom Broker after its latest quarterly results showed record revenue, wider margins and a surge in funded backlog.

Freedom Broker analysts Sergey Gilmanov and Zhanaidar Zulpaidar said Frequency Electronics’ long-term outlook improved after fiscal first-quarter 2027 operating margin reached 22.2% and funded backlog climbed to a record $129 million. However, they said expanding production capacity will take time and could require additional equity financing.

For investors, the downgrade reflects a valuation call rather than a deterioration in the business. Frequency Electronics is benefiting from growing demand for satellite systems and defense equipment, but its recent stock-price gains appear to reflect much of that opportunity. Capacity constraints, uneven program timing and possible shareholder dilution could limit near-term returns.

Satellite demand powers record quarter

Fiscal first-quarter revenue jumped 70% from a year earlier to a record $23.5 million, exceeding Freedom Broker’s estimate by 29% and the consensus forecast of $17.9 million by 31%.

Satellite revenue more than doubled to $11.8 million from $5.3 million and accounted for more than half of the company’s revenue growth. The analysts attributed the increase to faster execution of a satellite backlog that had been delayed near the end of the previous fiscal year.

Management indicated that Frequency Electronics is receiving follow-on orders and seeing additional opportunities in conventional satellite programs and newer satellite constellations.

Defense business rebounds

Revenue from non-space U.S. government and defense programs increased approximately 63% to $11.1 million from $6.9 million.

Freedom Broker said the rebound supports management’s argument that weakness in the preceding quarter largely reflected irregular program schedules rather than a drop in demand. Growth was supported by equipment for Patriot and Terminal High Altitude Area Defense, or THAAD, batteries, as well as demand for secure communications technology.

The timing of future revenue will depend partly on the company’s ability to add production capacity and align deliveries with customer schedules.

Profitability improves sharply

Gross profit more than doubled to $10.8 million from $5.1 million, while gross margin expanded to 45.8% from 36.8%.

Management attributed the improvement to greater labor utilization and better absorption of overhead as production increased. A more favorable sales mix and efficiency gains from maturing programs also helped.

Operating income climbed to $5.2 million from $400,000, lifting operating margin to 22.2% from 2.6%. Freedom Broker said the results suggest earlier investments in personnel and manufacturing are beginning to produce returns.

Management has also shown greater discipline in contract selection, including a willingness to reject work that does not meet profitability requirements. That approach could support the company’s longer-term goal of gross margins of at least 50%.

Forecasts and financing temper enthusiasm

Freedom Broker raised its fiscal 2027 earnings estimate to $1.45 a share from $1.37. Its fiscal 2028 estimate increased to $2.13 from $1.91, while its fiscal 2029 projection rose to $2.75 from $2.53.

The brokerage forecasts annual revenue of $83.4 million in fiscal 2027, $109 million in fiscal 2028 and $138 million in fiscal 2029. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization are projected to rise from $18.7 million to $38.5 million over the same period.

Those estimates point to meaningful growth, but the analysts cautioned that Frequency Electronics may need to issue stock to fund the capacity required to fulfill its expanding backlog. That could dilute current shareholders even if the spending supports higher revenue and earnings over time.

The combination of improving fundamentals and a sharply appreciated share price led Freedom Broker to raise its valuation while adopting a more cautious rating. Investors now must weigh a record backlog and expanding margins against execution demands, financing risk and expectations already embedded in the stock.

The brokerage raised its price target to $91 from $77. That represents potential upside of about 47% from the $62.06 share price cited in the firm’s Sept. 14 report.
